title: CEO drop-in: night fallback test & ops readiness - scratch
content:
Purpose: quick CEO drop-in (10 minutes max) for the weekly all-hands to acknowledge last night's degraded canary, explain immediate mitigations, and reinforce readiness posture. Tone: calm, factual, ownership-focused, appreciative of engineers + SRE on rapid mitigation. Not a postmortem — primary ask is to reassure and surface expectations for follow-ups.

Key context (one-sentence summary):
  - Overnight canary exercise surfaced a memory growth regression in the inference runtime (kernel selection path) under long-sequence streaming requests in eu-west-1. This triggered automatic fallback to CPU-backed instances for a subset of requests, increasing tail latency and temporarily spiking cost for the pilot traffic. We shifted traffic and rolled back the kernel tweak within 40 minutes.

CEO script (approx 2.5-3 minutes):
  - Opening (15s): "Hi everyone — quick drop-in about last night: our canary caught a problem in a recent runtime kernel change that impacted streaming latency for some requests in Europe. We acted quickly and contained it."
  - What happened (30s): "An optimization intended to improve memory layout for attention keys caused subtle memory growth in long-streaming sessions. During the canary we saw degraded tail latency and the system auto-routed impacted sessions to CPU fallbacks. That protected correctness but increased latency and cost."
  - Why this matters (20s): "Customers didn't experience data loss or incorrect outputs; they saw slower responses and we incurred higher infra cost for a short window. For a company built on predictable inference economics, that matters."
  - What we did (35s): "SRE and runtime immediately scaled targeted extra capacity, isolated the canary, rolled back the kernel change, and validated via synthetic replay. The rollback completed in ~40 minutes. Ops then ran a controlled re-test with improved telemetry."
  - Next steps & commitments (35s): "We will complete a focused postmortem (INC-3482) with a timeline in 48 hours, add a preflight test for long-sequence streaming to our canary suite, and add an automated regression gate for memory growth metrics. We'll also publish a short internal playbook so responders can reuse the exact actions we took."
  - Close (15s): "Huge thanks to the on-call SREs and runtime team — great work on containment. We'll follow up with details and action owners after the postmortem. Happy to take a single quick question, or you can drop questions in #ops-updates and we'll answer there."

Callouts for the executive moderator (Maya):
  - If anyone asks about customer impact: be explicit — no data loss, a small subset of pilot traffic saw 3–7x tail latency for ~40m. No CS escalations so far.
  - If asked about cost: call out that the CPU fallback is conservative and expensive; we'll tighten fallback policies after investigation.
  - If asked about recurrence: emphasize new regression gate & synthetic test added to canary pipeline.

Internal asks (prep list before drop-in):
  - Runtime: confirm rollback PR number + short summary of root cause (Ibrahim).
  - SRE: confirm exact timeline, metrics (p95/p99 tail latency delta), and which customers/pilot traffic segments saw the fallback (Lina).
  - Support/CS on standby: prepare a one-paragraph customer-facing blurb in case a pilot customer mentions speed issues.
  - Comms: draft internal thread and short follow-up email with links to postmortem, owners, and timeline.

Anticipated Q&A (concise answers for the CEO):
  Q1: "Did this impact our hosted customers or only the pilot?"
  A1: "Only pilot traffic in eu-west-1 used for the kernel experiment; no broad hosted customer impact detected. We monitored control groups closely."

  Q2: "Why did the fallback go to CPU instead of a warm GPU pool?"
  A2: "Fallback policy is conservative by design: if kernel-level memory behavior is anomalous we route to CPU to avoid crashes. We'll examine finer-grained fallback tiers so we can prefer nearby GPU variants when safe."

  Q3: "Is this an indicator the runtime is brittle?"
  A3: "No — it's a narrow regression from an optimization path. Our runtime is complex, which is why we have canaries; that system worked. We need to harden tests around long-sequence streaming which the canary missed."

  Q4: "How soon will customers see the protective changes?"
  A4: "We will add the memory-growth gate to the canary pipeline and deploy it within one week after validation. The fallback policy tuning will be an engineering sprint (2–3 weeks) to implement safely."

  Q5: "Any immediate changes to our release velocity?"
  A5: "No broad freeze. We will require an extra preflight check for long-streaming kernel changes; that affects a subset of runtime PRs, not platform-wide velocity."

  Q6: "Who owns the follow-up?"
  A6: "Inc owner: Ibrahim Khan (SRE) with runtime lead (Maya) as co-owner. Postmortem note and action owners will be in INC-3482."

Loose script cues / notes to self:
  - Keep language short, avoid technical deep dives — use "memory growth" instead of kernel internals unless someone asks.
  - Thank the responders by name during close.
  - Offer a short backlog item list to show concrete actions (canary gate, regression tests, fallback policy tuning).

Open questions / TODOs (fill before the drop-in):
  - Confirm exact p99 increase numbers for eu-west-1 synthetic traffic (SRE: Lina).
  - Get rollback PR link & short blurb for the follow-up email (Runtime: Ibrahim).
  - Draft internal follow-up email copy (Comms: Calvin) — short + links + owners + expected PM timeline.

Follow-up email draft (one-paragraph skeleton):
  "TL;DR: Last night a runtime kernel change caused memory growth in long-sequence streaming during a canary in eu-west-1. We rolled back the change in ~40m. No data loss; small subset pilot traffic saw increased tail latency and cost. Next: postmortem (INC-3482) in 48h, canary gate for memory growth in 1 week, fallback policy tuning in 2–3 weeks. Owners: Ibrahim (inc owner), Maya (runtime), Lina (SRE). Full details + links: [INC-3482] [rollback PR]."

Notes to self (tone & logistics):
  - Keep the drop-in tight. CEO should not apologize unnecessarily — be accountable and factual.
  - If the CEO invites technical questions, pass them immediately to runtime lead to avoid ad-libbing deep technical details.
  - After the all-hands, post the brief + links to #ops-updates and pin the post for 48 hours.

History / provenance (for traceability):
  - Raw logs & replay artifacts saved under: s3://redwood-ops/incident-3482/replay/
  - Canary job id: canary-eu-2025-04-21-09

—— end of scratch —
